experiences.G0: Single-pass execution: Once schema and workaround strategy are confirmed, bundle all filtering logic into one SQL statement (e.g., CTE); never run preview or duplicate queries before saving.
experiences.G1: Targeted schema exploration: When domain knowledge suggests a specific column name, query it directly with exact quoting before exhausting alternative schema searches or DISTINCT probes.
experiences.G2: Cheap filter verification: Run DISTINCT and COUNT(*) on filter columns before the main query; if LIMIT N returns fewer than N rows, check join coverage and NULL distribution immediately.
experiences.G3: Cast-verify before sort: Explicitly verify CAST succeeds and preview top values before trusting sort results on potentially string-typed numeric columns.
experiences.G4: Single LLM call: Craft one specific prompt with the full candidate list and a direct question; avoid retry loops that double token cost or cause refusals.
experiences.G5: Single-pass schema: Probe each table once (PRAGMA table_info or describe + preview); after confirming columns, stop — never repeat describe/preview/SELECT* on the same table.
experiences.G6: Hardcode known literals: Embed known values (coordinates, canonical names, FK/ID→name mappings) as SQL literals or CASE statements; never invoke LLM operators to recover dataset-specific precise facts.
experiences.G7: Commit early: Once schema is mapped and a query produces a result matching the simplest interpretation, output it immediately without re-deliberating on alternative definitions.
experiences.G8: Output shape verification: Before finalizing SQL, confirm expected output shape (per-record vs. aggregated) to avoid incorrectly collapsing rows with GROUP BY or AVG.
experiences.G9: Early cardinality check: Apply all SQL filters first and COUNT DISTINCT before invoking any LLM operator; pre-filter candidates with SQL to minimize row count and reduce per-row LLM token cost.
experiences.G10: Exhaust schema paths: Use information_schema upfront to find pre-computed or pre-aggregated summary columns matching the query metric; try PRAGMA and string parsing before any LLM operator.
experiences.G11: LLM-last resort: Exhaust all cheap SQL probes in ≤3 calls; never use llm_reduce as a world-knowledge oracle for dataset-specific counts — it produces wrong answers at non-trivial token cost.
experiences.G12: Spot-check LLM labels: Before applying llm_map to full tables (>100 rows), sample ~10 rows to validate classification accuracy and confirm no cheaper SQL path exists.
experiences.G13: Proxy breadth preference: Never substitute a proxy column without confirming its values map correctly to the target concept; wrong proxies produce confidently incorrect answers.
experiences.G14: Stable sort keys: When ORDER BY produces ties at LIMIT boundaries, always add a deterministic secondary sort key (e.g., primary ID or name ASC) to return exactly one unambiguous row.
experiences.G15: Early key normalization: Detect join key format mismatches upfront (e.g., LPAD for fixed-width codes) and fix atomically; confirm target record exists in the reference table before proceeding.
experiences.G16: SQL-first joins: When a reference table with matching IDs exists, attempt the JOIN directly in SQL before concluding data is absent and invoking costly LLM classification.
experiences.G17: Minimal-context LLM fallback: When a column is absent but derivable via SQL (e.g., URL concatenation or pattern), construct it deterministically first; only invoke LLM if no predictable pattern exists.
experiences.G18: Cardinality precision: When a query implies a single entity answer, filter to the single DB-linked record rather than unioning all historically associated records to avoid over-retrieval.
experiences.G19: LLM-setup validation: Check all required llm_map parameters (key_column, target, etc.) before the first call to eliminate costly repeated setup failures.
experiences.G20: URL-intent recognition: When a question asks where to find information, immediately query for a `url` or `link` column rather than returning data rows.
experiences.G21: Row-preview probe: Use `SELECT * LIMIT 1` or `PRAGMA table_info` immediately to reveal all columns including those with special characters that LIKE-based searches miss.
experiences.G22: Sample-then-aggregate: Sample one XML/text column first to confirm the pattern, then write the full aggregation query immediately rather than probing each column individually.
experiences.G23: Tie-check before commit: When finding a min/max aggregate, verify whether multiple rows share that extreme value before returning one result to avoid incorrect answers.
experiences.G24: Structural ID inference: When a lookup table has only an id column, check if its ID values encode range boundaries usable directly in the fact table to replace multi-step joins.
experiences.G25: Distinct-before-fallback: Prefer COUNT(DISTINCT key) over COUNT(*) when querying junction or denormalized tables to avoid overcounting duplicate rows.
experiences.G26: Denominator scope: For rate/completion queries, include ALL qualifying entries (e.g., DNQ) in the denominator; only explicitly matching statuses count in the numerator.
